correctness.rationale: For the regular odd polygon, the opposite-vertex geometry and the hyperbolic cosine law reconstruct the stated arc angle. Each boundary piece is a circle arc of radius \(d\), so its length is \(\alpha\sinh d\). Hyperbolic Gauss–Bonnet, with geodesic curvature \(\coth d\) on the arcs and the equal vertex turning contributions, gives \(A=n\alpha(1+\cosh d)-2\pi\). Algebra then yields the classical hyperbolic Barbier relation. Independent numerical reconstruction on odd orders from 3 through 101 reproduced the formulas and the fixed-width disk limit.

originality.rationale: Prior work establishes that hyperbolic Reuleaux polygons are bodies of constant width, and Santaló's classical hyperbolic Barbier theorem gives the general relation between area and perimeter for a constant-width body. Those results do not supply the separate perimeter and area of the regular odd-order Reuleaux family as explicit functions of \((n,d)\). The audited theorem computes the arc angle from the regular polygon geometry, obtains both exact invariants, and gives the fixed-width disk limit. The general Barbier relation is correctly treated as prior and recovered rather than re-claimed.
residual_risks: Santaló's 1945 full text was not directly readable in this run, so a historical explicit regular-polygon specialization remains a bibliographic risk.
The area–perimeter relation itself is classical and is not part of the originality claim.

final_claim: For every regular hyperbolic Reuleaux polygon of odd order \(n\ge3\) and width \(d>0\), the stated central arc angle \(\alpha(n,d)\) gives exact perimeter \(L=n\alpha\sinh d\) and area \(A=n\alpha(1+\cosh d)-2\pi\); equivalently \(A+2\pi=L\coth(d/2)\), and at fixed \(d\) the family converges in these invariants to the radius-\(d/2\) disk as \(n\to\infty\).
